name: annotation-organ-matching
title: Annotation-Based Organ Matching — SBML MIRIAM + BTO Crosswalk Provenance
question:
How does a BioModels entry get tagged with an HRA Uberon organ when the
match comes from its embedded SBML MIRIAM annotations rather than its
name — and which biological CVTerm qualifiers / ontologies actually carry
that organ signal?

study_card.goal: Summarize the committed annotation-based organ-matching catalog (datasets/biomodel_annotation_catalog.json, Task 4): how many models/organs it reaches, and, per organ tag, which biological qualifier and which ontology (Uberon/FMA/BTO) produced it -- transparently, down to the specific CVTerm.
study_card.mechanism: AnnotationMatchStep.update -> load_annotation_envelope(catalog_path) -> scan every biomodel_dos[].organs[].via entry (the SBML CVTerm hit: curie, biological qualifier, element) -> annotation_summary{n_ids, n_tagged, n_organs, qualifier_counts, ontology_counts} + sample_provenance -> RAMEmitter. Organ resolution itself (annotation_match.annotate_model) walks each model/compartment/species CVTerm, extracts an Uberon/FMA/BTO CURIE, and maps it to an HRA organ_index entry directly (Uberon/FMA) or via a curated 32-entry BTO->organ crosswalk (BTO terms, BRENDA Tissue Ontology, are what BioModels curators attach almost universally; direct Uberon/FMA hits are comparatively rare).
study_card.expected_result: The organ signal is dominated by BTO-mediated hits (via the crosswalk) rather than direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM matches, because BioModels curation practice annotates tissue/cell context with BTO far more often than with Uberon/FMA directly.
study_card.main_expert_question: Which biological qualifiers / ontologies carry the most organ signal?

biological_summary:
BioModels curators annotate SBML elements (the model itself, compartments,
species) with MIRIAM CVTerms: a biological qualifier (e.g. "is", "is part
of", "occurs in") plus a resource URI naming an ontology term. Very few
entries carry a direct Uberon/FMA anatomical term; most instead carry a
BRENDA Tissue Ontology (BTO) term describing the cell line, tissue sample,
or assay context the model was parameterized against. `annotation_match.py`
extracts every such CVTerm hit, and where it's BTO, resolves it to an HRA
Uberon organ via a curated 32-entry BTO->organ crosswalk
(`datasets/bto_uberon_crosswalk.json`) -- this crosswalk is *the* mechanism
that makes BTO-heavy BioModels annotation practice usable as organ
evidence at all; without it, only the rare direct Uberon/FMA hits would
resolve.
readouts: annotation_summary.n_ids / n_tagged (catalog envelope: corpus size, organ-tagged count)
annotation_summary.ontology_counts (ontology prefix -> hit count: BTO vs UBERON/FMA)

report.title: Annotation Organ Matching — 114/1,096 models, 14 organs, driven almost entirely by BTO
report.objective:
How does annotation-based organ matching work mechanically, and which
qualifiers/ontologies actually carry the organ signal?
report.conclusion:
The committed annotation catalog (`datasets/biomodel_annotation_catalog.json`)
tags 114/1,096 models (10.4%) with an HRA organ across 14 distinct
organs. Of the 168 individual CVTerm hits behind those tags, 156 (92.9%)
resolve via a BTO term through the curated 32-entry BTO->organ
crosswalk, and only 12 (7.1%) resolve via a direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM
match -- confirming BTO is overwhelmingly the dominant anatomy signal in
BioModels' own curation practice (278 models in the corpus carry a BTO
term at all; the crosswalk is what turns that into organ evidence). By
biological qualifier, `BQB_OCCURS_IN` (88 hits) and `BQB_IS` (40 hits)
dominate, with `BQB_IS_VERSION_OF` (35), `BQB_IS_PART_OF` (4), and
`BQB_HAS_PART` (1) trailing -- curators overwhelmingly express anatomy as
"this model occurs in / is this tissue" rather than compositional
part-of relationships.
report.caveat:
The BTO->organ crosswalk is a curated 32-entry mapping, not a complete
BTO->Uberon bridge -- BTO terms outside that crosswalk contribute
nothing, so the 92.9% BTO-hit share measures the crosswalk's reach
within the catalog it produced, not BTO's full potential organ signal
across the corpus. Extending the crosswalk is the most direct lever to
raise `annotation-recall-gain`'s coverage numbers further.

bto-crosswalk-dominates.observed: BTO-via-crosswalk dominates the organ signal: >=90% of CVTerm hits resolve through the curated BTO->organ crosswalk vs direct Uberon/FMA (observed 156/168 = 92.9% BTO, 12 = 7.1% direct).

corpus-organ-coverage.observed: Annotation matching tags ~10% of the corpus across >10 organs (observed 114/1,096 = 10.4% models, 14 distinct organs).

occurs-in-is-qualifiers-dominate.observed: Occurrence/identity qualifiers dominate over compositional ones (observed BQB_OCCURS_IN 88 + BQB_IS 40 vs BQB_IS_PART_OF 4 + BQB_HAS_PART 1 of 168 hits).

prerequisites.rationale: Scans the SBML MIRIAM/BTO annotations of the same 1,096-model BioModels corpus biomodel-hra-map harvests; the BTO->organ crosswalk resolves them to the HRA organ set.

findings.statement:
Of the 168 CVTerm hits behind the annotation catalog's 114 organ-tagged
models, 156 (92.9%) resolve through the curated BTO->organ crosswalk
and only 12 (7.1%) through a direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM match --
BTO-via-crosswalk is the dominant, not incidental, organ-matching
mechanism, and `BQB_OCCURS_IN`/`BQB_IS` are the dominant qualifiers
(88 and 40 of 168 hits).

evidence.summary: ontology_counts: BTO 156, UBERON 12; qualifier_counts: BQB_OCCURS_IN 88, BQB_IS 40, BQB_IS_VERSION_OF 35, BQB_IS_PART_OF 4, BQB_HAS_PART 1; 114/1,096 models tagged (10.4%), 14 organs.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline annotation-organ-matching composite (committed catalog scan) completed without error.

biological_validation.basis: The qualifier/ontology breakdown matches expected BioModels curation practice: tissue/cell-line context (BTO) is annotated far more often than direct anatomical ontology terms (Uberon/FMA), and 'occurs in'/'is' qualifiers dominate over compositional part-of relationships.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 makes the annotation-matching mechanism transparent and falsifiable: the BTO->organ crosswalk, not direct Uberon/FMA annotation, is what does 92.9% of the work, directly motivating crosswalk-extension as the next lever (see annotation-recall-gain).

limitations: The 32-entry BTO->organ crosswalk is curated, not exhaustive -- BTO terms it doesn't cover contribute zero organ signal, so the 92.9% BTO share is a lower bound on BTO's true anatomical relevance in this corpus.
sample_provenance surfaces only the first 10 organ-tagged models for spot-checking, not a systematic precision audit of every hit.

resolved_uncertainties: BTO-mediated matching (via the curated crosswalk), not direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM annotation, is the dominant organ-tagging mechanism in this BioModels corpus (156 vs 12 hits).
remaining_uncertainties: How much more organ coverage would extending the 32-entry BTO->organ crosswalk unlock, given 278 corpus models carry a BTO term at all vs the 114 that currently resolve to an organ?

followup_study_proposals.title: BTO->organ crosswalk extension
followup_study_proposals.motivation: 278 models carry a BTO term but only 114 resolve to an organ through the current 32-entry crosswalk; extending the crosswalk against the remaining BTO terms in the corpus could raise annotation-based organ-tagging recall further.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Enumerate the distinct BTO terms present across all 278 BTO-annotated corpus models, identify which are absent from the current 32-entry crosswalk, and curate organ mappings for the highest-frequency gaps.
